0.1.n: Makes the question polite; the item being discussed is left unstated.

0.2.n: Placed at the end to make a polite question.

1.1.n: Makes the question polite; the item being discussed is left unstated.

1.2.n: Placed at the end to make a polite question.

2.0.n: Refers to an item near the speaker or one they are pointing out.

2.1.n: Marks これ as the thing the speaker wants shown.

2.2.n: 見せて is the て-form of 見せる; adding ください makes a polite request.

3.0.n: Refers to an item near the speaker or one they are pointing out.

3.1.n: Marks これ as the thing the speaker wants shown.

3.2.n: 見せて is the て-form of 見せる; adding ください makes a polite request.

4.0.n: Refers to the item the speaker has chosen.

4.1.n: Marks これ as the item being requested.

4.2.n: After a noun plus を, this politely requests an item.

5.0.n: Refers to the item the speaker has chosen.

5.1.n: Marks これ as the item being requested.

5.2.n: After a noun plus を, this politely requests an item.

0.tip: Japanese can leave out the item when it is clear what you are asking about.

1.tip: Japanese can leave out the item when it is clear what you are asking about.

2.tip: A verb in the て-form followed by ください makes a polite request to do something.

3.tip: A verb in the て-form followed by ください makes a polite request to do something.

4.tip: これをください is a standard way to ask for an item you want to buy.

5.tip: これをください is a standard way to ask for an item you want to buy.
